Better dead than Red! And since it’s either kill or be killed, you will be the untimely demise of Reds aplenty. It is really surprising how a seemingly simple idea can turn into a success story. Even more so, considering the rookie dev team (with a rather uninspired name, to boot).  Still, the game represents a brilliant example of quality independent gaming and thinking outside the box at the same time.
In the absence of a cohesive plotline, players have to contend with a seemingly randomized succession of stages which always increase the stakes in terms of survivability. To better understand this game, you must first summarize it at the most basic level. What are you representing in this particular title? You are not only a silent, nameless and genderless protagonist but you appear to be the remedy to the software/digital illusion game world which I might compare to The Matrix. You control a black figure, statue, firewall personification (call it what you will) that must battle and defeat countless scores of “Red Dudes” as the game itself refers to your foes. I consider them the inherent problem that needs to be solved, the viruses which plague a literal immaculate environment (all the backgrounds are white). Maybe I’m going too far in the pursuit of finding reason where there is none to be found. But I thoroughly enjoy chromatic aberrations and contrasts as they break the mold of conventional graphical representation. SUPERHOT contains just 4 colors (also their shades, if you want to go into detail): White, Red, Black and the occasional Yellow.
If you thought the gameplay itself is unconventional, you’ll be pleased to find out that even the main menu draws attention to itself. You have a faux jailbreak/communication interface which simulates the discussions between two hackers dealing with warez. Funny dialogues about barely being able to crack the game and having to deal with password protected files. It’s all very meta and it might even add a dash of black humor for those which actually play a pirated copy of the game. I honestly hope they don't. Spectacular titles such as SUPERHOT don’t deserve to be stolen by any gamer. Save up cash, wait for a Steam Sale, do what you want but stop pirating software. It’s 2017 and digital distribution platforms have made gaming more affordable than ever.
All this talk beating around the bush and you’d think I’m gonna pass the chance to explain to you, exactly what makes SUPERHOT so special and unique? It’s time manipulation, folks. The aforementioned Matrix franchise and also the Max Payne video game series have popularized this visual effect in contemporary times. As the game so eloquently puts it in its tutorial level, “Time Moves Only When You Move”. From this relatively straightforward gameplay mechanic, the entire action and entertenment value of SUPERHOT tip the odds in its favor. Shooting and dodging bullets in real time, would have already represented 99.9% of shooters out there. Gun and melee fights gain a new tactical layer as you can plan your next move under the safety of a slow motion effect which let’s you see the enemy projectiles racing towards you and have the chance of avoiding them while taking precise aim at your assailants.
A large enough arsenal which contains both firearms, swords, baseball bats and even regular objects which range from bottles to TV sets, can be used to cause deadly harm upon the Red Dudes. It doesn’t even matter where you shoot them, for example. They break apart (more specifically shatter as if made from glass) even if they get shot in the limbs. Headhshots while spectacular, shall earn you the Achievement “Pointless but cool”. Many more challenges await to materialize in the form of creative kills while using the stage objects and backgrounds to your advantage. In the end, Black Dude (or Dudette) shall always win against the Reds since it is controlled by something unrivalled yet by artificial intelligence in terms of quick reflexes: the human mind.
The lack of a multiplayer component to SUPERHOT seems like a missed opportunity, even if I’m never one to care for the inclusion of MP. I reckon many amongst my readers would have enjoyed sparring against each other, in this title. All my metaphors aside, SUPERHOT is simply fun to play whether you have a lot of spare time on hand or if you desire a  short gaming session to unwind from daily stress. Aforementioned Achievements and Cards ensure that absolutely all types of Steam collectors shall be satisfied. But honestly I would have recommended this game with my perfect rating, regardless by the presence of any Steam auxiliaries. SUPERHOT is a fine chapter within independent gaming’s proud book of accomplishments!
+ Excellent visual style.
+ Entertaining gameplay with a twist of its own.
+ Replayability factor, considering the game’s open-ended structure.
+ Steam Achievements & Trading Cards.
- None worth mentioning.

If you enjoy narrative based games with thought-provoking content and/or dialogue, you will probably like this game. I loved it and found it remarkably beautiful. Yet despite how much I liked it, I genuinely am not sure whether I can recommend it or not.
The game is a compilation of mini-games made by a friend of TBG's narrator, Davey Wreden. This friend is identified by the name Coda. Coda's games are quite personal, and The Beginner's Guide tells a story about Wreden's relationship with Coda via the games. The organization of the games and the narration weaves a beautiful story, every point of which I enjoyed in some way or another.
However...
Partway into the game it becomes clear that Coda does not want his games to be played. Players of the game discover that they are not intended for others and that he does not want Wreden showing them to other people. If you want more details about this, go read 3rd party reviews. As a random person without access to Coda, I have no idea what he really wants. But if he is creating his games for himself, and not for others, then by purchasing this compliation of his games and promoting it, I/we may be fueling Wreden's and Coda's problems that are discussed in TBG. Had I known more about this, I probably would not have purchased the game.

Five Nights at Freddy's is a different game than most horror games. It behaves much differently; instead of moving around, you sit in an office and fend off the killer animatronics which is a brilliant idea, but it does get a little old once you play again. The game has an amazing backstory that produces tons of theories and the game is 3D modeled spectacularly with a great sense of fear and atmosphere built straight into the players mind when playing. The only way of knowing what to do in the game is the Phone Guy, a earlier nightwatchman who sends the player phone messages to tell the player what to do to avoid being killed. But the phone guy doesn't list everything you need to watch out for, making half the game unpredictable except its jumpscares.
Story:
Five Nights at Freddy's has a deep story but isn't completely visible to the player, the story is mentioned one time by the phone guy, and the rest is hidden deep inside the game itself. You need to pay close attention to the building to find out the general basis of the story. And even though the story is all but theories; what we know so far is disgusting, gory, and inhumane.
It's brilliant.
Verdict:
Five Nights at Freddy's successfully tries to be different than most other horror games, and it does it well. It produces tons of fear, and a GREAT story which other horror games lack. The game has tons of features that do lots to scare and surprise the player. Although the game is great, the jumpscares get a little old and are completely predictable once you mess something up. Even though there is a lot of flaws; this game is brilliant and if you love horror you need to play this.
Rating:
9.5/10.
+ Great Story
+ Different than most other horror games in a good way.
+ Scary Jumpscares
+ Awesome Features
- Game gets a little old through time.

Chroma Squad... what a unusual concept.
I grew up watching oldschool japanese films (Godzilla, Ultraman, Rodan, etc), watching shows like Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, oldschool martial arts films that were dubbed by... less than stellar actors, etc.
So lets just say I love the source material and whatnot.
Final Fantasy Tactics style games (Tactical RPGs) are always sorta hit or miss.  Some focus too much on choice leaving you with a mountain of options and a hard time deciding what actually works for you.  Others are far too focused on the story and ignore a good tactical format for combat.
Chroma Squad hits alot of good notes:
-5 classes, all with tie-ins with character archtypes in shows like MMPR
-"Actors" that give different stat boosts to the class you slot them into, or to your progress as a whole, depending on choice.
-Solid combat that feels good, without a mountain of stats and rules to learn
-Various mini-goals for each 'mission' (part of an eppisode) that are typically not too hard to complete and net you more money to spend on upgrades
-MMO style gear levels (White/Green/Blue/Purple) that help you determine which gear is better (not to mention easy to understand stats)
-Alot of comedy moments before/during/and after each fight.  There are more references to pop culture, source material, and strange happenings than I can even begin to list.
-Great badguys, even when they are repetative it's still funny to see the dialog that tries to explain why they are there.
Now some negatives
-Crafting system can turn out garbage gear.  You can break said gear down and try again, but it's a losing system.
-Some of the 'mini-missions' don't work with everyones playstyle, there have been a few so far that I found irritating to try to complete.
-Sometimes the 'jump' feature doesn't seem to want to fire for no reason.  This makes positioning annoying at times.
-Music gets repetative, but not really a big issue, mute works wonders.
I love me a good tactical game, and one filled with humor and references to some of the best (and cheesiest if I'm honest) shows/movies is awesome in my book.  Too bad there isn't multiplayer co-op or pvp, that would send this game to the realm of 'zomg best timewaster ever... for a week or three'

Chroma Squad is an outstanding tactical RPG that I highly recommend to anyone who is a fan of Super Sentai, Kamen Rider and a ton of other live action hero shows. The game clocks in about 15 hours (give or take) to complete one play through and is loaded with a ton of fan service and pop culture references that keep you constantly hyped and laughing throughout your journey. The blend of simulation and RPG is where the game truly shines and feels unique. You aren't only creating your dream Sentai team, you are a part of the show!
On the tactical side, the game does not get very complex, and I found the game to be quite a breeze on Normal, but honestly, that's okay. A game does not need to be hard as hell in order to be fun. However, I will note that as hype as the Mecha battles are they are pretty one sided and easy to complete most of the time. From the perspective of a fan of Sentai it makes total sense and you feel awesome beating up Kaiju for the sake of justice, but the above mentioned simplicity is why I couldn't recommend the game to someone just looking for a Tactical RPG fix. Though I would say at the very least look up some footage and if you are open minded enough you might really enjoy it anyways! Might even get you interested into Sentai etc.
Chroma Squad as it is may have relatively simple combat, crafting and business simulation but I strongly feel like that's the entire point of the game. The game doesn't just want you to create a Sentai show, it wants you to be the hero! So what are you waiting for? Get out there and deliver some justice! And don't forget to shout a cheesy line like "Justice is best served in a rainbow of colors!" It doesn't have to make sense, as long as you do a cool pose while saying it you'll be FINE.

•	Amazing retro graphics
Cons

•	Left me begging for more customization. (perhaps we might see more in updates)
•	A few annoying bugs, but patches should be coming in quite soon
9/10

Let's get all of this clear. I played over twenty hours in the Beta, and it refused me to play any more (Apparently my Beta time ran out). However, throughout EVERY hour of this game, I was finding new ways to play, new tricks to try and new methods to win the round. I had only played TWO different classes. Trapper and Monster. Only TWO! I can't imagine what else I could have learnt about the game if only I had played MORE! I played twenty hours and was still stuck on how Daisy worked! When I first saw gameplay and trailers I was insistent on how un-re-playable it seemed. I stuck around though, I entered for the Beta and as I mentioned earlier I was hooked. "Wow, that looked pretty epic!" and "I wonder if they would fall for..." was coming out of my mouth at least once EACH round! They say in the "Evacuation" tutorial  (tutorial for the "Evacuation" gamemode) that there are, and I quote, "...over 800,000 possible combinations for the ultimate in replayability." That's the so-called "Campaign" of Evolve! There are something like five gamemodes at the moment (if you weren't blind enough to read the text if you chose the "Evacuation" gamemode, then you would know this. Not to mention the amount of tutorials they had already released in the "Tutorials" section, which displayed information about all the gamemodes that were going to be available on release). So for all you whiners out there about how "boring" it is and how you "Got bored after two hours" and how that must have had an oh so terrible impact on your life, keep reading, it gets even better!
I also read in a lot of the "Thumbs Down" reviews that the game is "...multiplayer only". For your information, I have just tested the single-player (completely offline, disconnected from the wifi offline) and I almost got my teeth kicked in by a bunch of "Normal" difficulty bots (I tried both teams). You can play not only Evacuation mode, but also any other game-mode that you wish (ready?) OFFLINE and still have a hell of a challenge to it! If you had only stopped to understand that when you get access to the open Beta for a game such as this (a game designed to play online with OTHER people) that the developers must evaluate how the game operates under stress! Of course there are going to be a hell of a lot of bugs, of course there are going to be faulty optimizations. THIS IS WHAT A BETA IS FOR! So that you may tell them that there are bugs and so that they may fix them. I found over thirteen little "glitches" in the Beta, one included a little bug where if you tried to climb a wall and the dome fell right in front of you as you went mid-animation to climb, you would simply slide down the wall and get stuck halfway inside the dome. When it was released yesterday, I immediately went to try it out, and well, FIXED! (Same place, probably not the exact same time in the animation but it was definitely within the time frame needed to get me stuck) Stop complaining about bugs if all you did was play the Beta in hopes for it to be perfect!
Okay, one thing I must sit on the fence about, is the DLC costs. I agree that it costs too much, but I disagree that it's enough to make you not buy the game. Firstly, because the DLC does not add ANY bonuses other than Aesthetics and "Different Characters". Ok cool, different characters, great, mhm. You don't NEED them. At all. Whatsoever. Nobody said to you that "in order to play this game you have to buy all the DLC" or "in order to enjoy the game you have to buy all the DLC". Not a single person but those who didn't bother READING what the DLC actually IS. The tier system in the game DOES NOT, I say again, DOES NOT give you access to new monsters and characters because they're "stronger". It gives you access to them, to keep you playing the game. To find new play styles and combinations and weaknesses and strengths and opportunities where one person's ability might come useful, where yours currently isn't. That doesn't mean that you will completely forget the first character you used in a certain class. No, instead I went BACK to the original character because her toolkit suited my playstyle!
Sorry for the fairly long post everybody, but I just hope that this clears any doubts that you may have had about the game, be it with "Singleplayer" issues or "Bugs" or "DLC". If you have anymore questions then feel free to contact me through this account or send me an email at
Thankyou for reading and go slay some monsters!

This is very much in the vein of traditional point-and-click style games like the Monkey Island series. If you're into the kind of puzzles that you play in games like that (including sometimes frustrating video game logic), you'll find this to be a delightful game. In fact, I think a lot of the puzzles and logical conclusions you have to make to reach solutions in this game are actually much more straightforward (and aha!-inducing) than a lot of the puzzles in traditional point-and-clicks.
There's a lot of fun humor in these games, and a lot of moving back and forth between areas and basking in your own cleverness when you've finally solved a puzzle. The art and music style is Afro-Caribbean as others have pointed out, and apparently many of the character profiles are based on African masks, which is pretty neat. It's also cool to have a video game that features neary all African characters--I mean how often do you see that? If all of this sounds good to you, then I totally recommend getting this game.

As a rule, I hate survival games.
I couldn't stand Rust,  The Forest,   Ark,  none of them.  They all advertise "survival", but they just boil down to getting murdered by other players, or wandering around empty areas looking for junk to collect.  So I had low expectations for this,  but I was always curious about it.  Something about the graphical style, and the sense of isolation I got from the screenshots.  Well the summer sale rolled around, and my hand was forced.
To my astonishment ... I don't hate this survival game!
It portrays,  (what feels like, at least) an accurate representation of being stranded in the Canadian wilderness with nothing but the boots on your feet.  Heck, even those fall apart the further you walk in them.
To survive, you must sprint between abandoned cabins, through long stretches of hostile forest, or wind swept frozen lakes. There are multiple threats along the way in the form of bears and wolves.  But the most deadly threat of all is the weather.  Go out into a blizzard without the proper clothing and you will be freezing to death in seconds.  Add to this that once health is lost, it is not easily regained.  You could be well fed, and warm enough, but if you are dehydrated don't expect that your condition is going to magically improve.
There are other brilliant mechanics like the inherent dilemna of finding a book that you can read to improve your cooking or weapon handling skills, but which also provides excellent kindling for a fire.  Kindling is almost always in short supply, so you will find yourself torn between the urge to skill up, and the need to survive.  It's clever stuff.
Only played a few hours of this, but I expect I will be playing many more.  Long Dark, you have given me hope for the survival genre!

Play a multiplayer game of cat and mouse in the Skirmish Hunt game mode, 4v1.
The game is all about misdirection and luring or pushing your opponent into a corner.
The hunters will quickly be turned into the hunted within a few minutes of the games.
There is a high tension when playing as a lone monster against 4 players. It may feel daunting to take on 4 players alone. However, this tension eases as you grow stronger over time. And it comes with an overwhelming sense of satisfaction when demolishing the other players.
The hunter's focus is mainly on tracking and cornering the monster. Speed, teamwork and tactics is key here to prevent the monster in growing too strong and overtaking the hunters in brute strength. Such as the monster will lose all its armor as it evolves onto its next stage.
The Skirmish Hunt game mode's strength, or perhaps fault, lies in it's competitive design. It does not give a lot of slack for un-even matched teams. A poor match making can end a game under 4 minutes. While most average matches last under 10 minutes. You can clearly see the distance between skill levels within a minute of the game, and can leave the player feeling hopeless as a hunter or overwhelmed with the pressure as a monster.
The other game mode available during launch, is Evacuation. This is a series of 5 matches, where the outcome of the previous match will roll over to the next as perks. Such as AI soldiers or monster minions to aid the player. The game balances this out by giving the losing team a handicap base stats buff, so it isn't an unfair advantage to the winning team.
Playing a full series of 5 matches in Evacuation can last between 40 to 60 minutes. It includes the Hunting game mode, while adding three other new play objectives. An escort mission, seek and destroy mission, defend mission. The Evacuation match starts with a Hunt and ends with a Defend mission. In between, the players get to vote which one to play after each round ends.
This game has finesse to it, there is a lot to be aware of at once.
Going into further details, a match always has 1 main monster and 1 of each hunter role. That means you can't have an entire team of assault. Nor is there a game mode yet that supports larger players matches, such as there isn't a mode for 2v8.
The hunter classes and roles are broken up as such,
Healer, Support, Trapper, Assault.
The monsters classes play style varies by melee, range, and speed. You can think of them being a soldier, archer, and rogue. But the all of them have the basics of sneaking, smelling, climbing, and a version of dashing.
Going down the laundry list of things in the game;
As for the current options for DLC, there's only vanity skins for your characters and weapons
So as far as the paid DLC goes, the only thing that caught my eye is the cost to buy 4 new hunters. Having unlocked all the monsters and hunters, I can tell that each one has it's own play style and feel to it. It's to your own benefit to know what each character can and cannot do. This quickly reminds me of how each DoTA or LoL character benefits from having a large roaster of characters to choose from. Whether of Evolve is trying to head towards that design of a large character roaster, I can't say for sure.

My personal opinion on the trilogy:
Pro:
- beautiful animation
- great character design
- fantastic music
- the 2nd episode had lovely and funny sections, much more than the others
- Bozo lashing out at Rufus
Cons:
- self-aware AND non-self-aware unfunny sexism: despite the voluntary crassness of the interaction with female characters, it's easy to notice that in general, women in this game are either non-interactive background or full-on clichés/plot devices. I'm struggling to remember any woman playing a somewhat neutral role such as vendor, therapist, journalist... the ones we see working are part of the main cast and mostly fall into tired female tropes.
- self-aware unfunny racism. See Rock Paper Shotgun article and other comments
- the writer(s) built a somewhat consistent character, but not a consistent world: friends and foes are mostly differenciated by their aptitude to put up with the main character, which is very high for both, despite all logic. The world does not react to the main character in general, making his antics tiring by the third episode rather than entertaining. We can't empathise with the character nor can we with the world, which is the shame.
- Not only the main character doesn't change throughout the series, but his actions become more selfish and tasteless as the story progresses.
- deus ex machina explanation which binds the whole story together
- disappointing ending.
Overall, I felt that the first episode was suprinsingly charming, because of the discovery of the great design, animation, music and somewhat original setting; the second introduced great new areas, clearer puzzles, and more funny moments even though the character becomes a bit tiring and his actions more cringe-worthy; by the third I no longer felt like investing myself heavily into the world and puzzles and I cringed much more than I laughed, both due to tasteless scenes and bad story.
This is a no for me.

I finished Bioshock some days ago and I loved it!
Bioshock endured the test of time very well.
The story is just as good today as it was 7 years ago, and it's a very good story.

I also enjoyed the evolution from sort-of horror-ish in the early game to full fps. It sort of makes sense, because when you arrive you are weak and stumbling in the dark.
You don't know what's going on. So it should be scary.
But as you get stronger and learn, it should get less and less scary.
About the graphics, they are a bit aged, but honestly, this game has such a unique and beautiful art style that the 7 year old graphics didn't even bother me.
I thoroughly enjoyed exploring every nook and corner of the city and in quite a few places I stopped and went like:
Wow. That is really cool.
Anyway, this is a great game, I enjoyed it very much, and I recommend it to anyone who likes first person shooters.

SUPERHOT
Released
SUPERHOT Team
SUPERHOT Team
3D First Person Shooter

25th of February, 2016

Singleplayer
Better dead than Red! And since it’s either kill or be killed, you will be the untimely demise of Reds aplenty. It is really surprising how a seemingly simple idea can turn into a success story. Even more so, considering the rookie dev team (with a rather uninspired name, to boot).  Still, the game represents a brilliant example of quality independent gaming and thinking outside the box at the same time.
In the absence of a cohesive plotline, players have to contend with a seemingly randomized succession of stages which always increase the stakes in terms of survivability. To better understand this game, you must first summarize it at the most basic level. What are you representing in this particular title? You are not only a silent, nameless and genderless protagonist but you appear to be the remedy to the software/digital illusion game world which I might compare to The Matrix. You control a black figure, statue, firewall personification (call it what you will) that must battle and defeat countless scores of “Red Dudes” as the game itself refers to your foes. I consider them the inherent problem that needs to be solved, the viruses which plague a literal immaculate environment (all the backgrounds are white). Maybe I’m going too far in the pursuit of finding reason where there is none to be found. But I thoroughly enjoy chromatic aberrations and contrasts as they break the mold of conventional graphical representation. SUPERHOT contains just 4 colors (also their shades, if you want to go into detail): White, Red, Black and the occasional Yellow.
If you thought the gameplay itself is unconventional, you’ll be pleased to find out that even the main menu draws attention to itself. You have a faux jailbreak/communication interface which simulates the discussions between two hackers dealing with warez. Funny dialogues about barely being able to crack the game and having to deal with password protected files. It’s all very meta and it might even add a dash of black humor for those which actually play a pirated copy of the game. I honestly hope they don't. Spectacular titles such as SUPERHOT don’t deserve to be stolen by any gamer. Save up cash, wait for a Steam Sale, do what you want but stop pirating software. It’s 2017 and digital distribution platforms have made gaming more affordable than ever.
All this talk beating around the bush and you’d think I’m gonna pass the chance to explain to you, exactly what makes SUPERHOT so special and unique? It’s time manipulation, folks. The aforementioned Matrix franchise and also the Max Payne video game series have popularized this visual effect in contemporary times. As the game so eloquently puts it in its tutorial level, “Time Moves Only When You Move”. From this relatively straightforward gameplay mechanic, the entire action and entertenment value of SUPERHOT tip the odds in its favor. Shooting and dodging bullets in real time, would have already represented 99.9% of shooters out there. Gun and melee fights gain a new tactical layer as you can plan your next move under the safety of a slow motion effect which let’s you see the enemy projectiles racing towards you and have the chance of avoiding them while taking precise aim at your assailants.
A large enough arsenal which contains both firearms, swords, baseball bats and even regular objects which range from bottles to TV sets, can be used to cause deadly harm upon the Red Dudes. It doesn’t even matter where you shoot them, for example. They break apart (more specifically shatter as if made from glass) even if they get shot in the limbs. Headhshots while spectacular, shall earn you the Achievement “Pointless but cool”. Many more challenges await to materialize in the form of creative kills while using the stage objects and backgrounds to your advantage. In the end, Black Dude (or Dudette) shall always win against the Reds since it is controlled by something unrivalled yet by artificial intelligence in terms of quick reflexes: the human mind.
The lack of a multiplayer component to SUPERHOT seems like a missed opportunity, even if I’m never one to care for the inclusion of MP. I reckon many amongst my readers would have enjoyed sparring against each other, in this title. All my metaphors aside, SUPERHOT is simply fun to play whether you have a lot of spare time on hand or if you desire a  short gaming session to unwind from daily stress. Aforementioned Achievements and Cards ensure that absolutely all types of Steam collectors shall be satisfied. But honestly I would have recommended this game with my perfect rating, regardless by the presence of any Steam auxiliaries. SUPERHOT is a fine chapter within independent gaming’s proud book of accomplishments!

The game 'Blood and Bacon' - developed by Big Corporation - is lighthearted, challenging at times and the best shooter type for groups of people. Blood and Bacon appears to be one of those games where the graphic design is put aside - mainly focusing on the content. This game did not fail to deliver content at all while maintaining an aesthetic. From the first impressions to the overall design, the mechanics of the game allowed for an easy-to-play style shooter.
Entering the game, it was obvious that Blood and Bacon would not be another highly-strung shooter. Immediately, I was overcome with a relaxed and joyous feeling. Met by a man speared to the back wall of his barn, there was already an idea of a lack of realism. The animation and design of the game follow a low-grade aesthetic with what seems like a permanent low-texture quality. In addition to this 'aesthetic', the movement of the man in the barn's face was sloppy as he spoke. This was somewhat pleasing as the developers put an equal amount of design into the landscape, objects and characters.
The map design is simple and easy to remember - this also made it difficult to avoid the oncoming stampedes of these monstrous creatures. Though there are a couple of houses placed around the map, there is no way to enter them. On top of this design, the animals were able to jump (or glitch?) onto the top of buildings, forcing the player to be contantly running in order to survive. This is what created the challenge.
The playable characters - according the the Blood and Bacon wikia - include:
- Johnny Blood - your generic well-built white male
- Lando Bacon - your generic well-built black male
- Creaky Skelly - a washed up dead cowboy
- Daisy Dee - a Lara Croft doppleganger
- Dead Viking - a viking?
With these characters comes a variety of weapons such as:
- Ak-47
- Shotgun
- Uzi
- P90
- M16
- The Mirv - a rocket launcher?
- Starting Pistol
- Revolver
- Silenced Pistol
- Paintball Gun
The characters and weaponry appeared to be equal with variety and design to the entire game.
In light of the design of the map, followed by the variety of characters and weaponry, this games succession becomes clear. The less serious atmosphere made 'Blood and Bacon' enjoyable for a large spectrum of gamers; including me, someone who does not enjoy FPS. It is most enjoyable with others as it is less interesting when played solo style. Overall, this game was well made and deserves all of the positive reviews it has recieved.

This game was available on a free promotion, so I picked it up as I had heard good things about it (and seen brief snippets of gameplay footage). However, I wasn't prepared for the amazing experience of this stylish, dark, pull-no-punches puzzle/platformer. In style and mood, I was actually most reminded of the film Eraserhead (and commiserations if you've ever seen it - it's brilliant, but not what many would call a pleasant experience). Apart from a couple of cheap deaths (and I do mean cheap), the vast majority of the puzzles are expertly presented, providing you with subtle hints to their solution without a single word of text explanation or spoken dialogue. There are only a couple that might be a little frustrating, but perseverance and experimentation will reward you. The sound design is fantastic, presenting you with ambient sounds to match the environments as well as aural cues when events and actions matter - and they perfectly complement the visual mood. The art design is superb - the seemingly minimalist presentation actually reveals an incredible sense of depth thanks to masterfully crafted and animated backgrounds.
In short, it's a masterpiece, and had I known then what I know now, I wouldn't have picked it up on a free promotion - I would have paid for it a long, long time ago. It's not long - probably about 3-4 hours in total - but the level of polish is something to be experienced. Plus, there is a brutally difficult secret level, which, if you can find it, presents you with hard platform challenges and then ramps up the difficulty to 11.
On the strength of this I will definitely be picking up "Inside", which looks even better.

Go Go Po... Chroma Rangers!
If you grew up, like me, watching the Power Rangers or any Japanese Super Sentai, it's probably worth a look.
The game use a nice pixel artstyle with a lot of color... lot of chroma!
As far as I know, it's the first Super Sentai Simulator and the two years wait since the kickstarter was worth it.
There is a story to follow so it's not a sim per say but you have some freedom with the customization of your squad and studio.
The game fit perfectly in the Super Sentai genre with crazy weird monsters, lots of weird poses and a good amount of friendships and conflicts. There is also some references to other games or memes that can be hit or miss but most of the game is spent in battle or getting ready to battle in the studio. Only a few story scenes are long, most are short unless they are important to the main plot.
The Teamwork mechanic is interesting and add a good amount of strategies to the tactical gameplay. On the normal difficulty, you can go all in like the Rangers usual do and barely win or take your time and overwhelm the baddies. Only as few battle may force you to pick a more specific strategy.
My first playthrough took me about 14 hours on the normal difficulty and, at this time, there are 3 different endings with a few different stages depending on the path taken. Except a few specific choices, the game is linear.
Oh and there are Mecha/Kaiju battles! They are pretty simple but you can't have Super Sentai without monsters growing with those slow battles full of sparks!
This review was inspired by Chroma Squad that was inspired by Saban's Power Rangers that was inspired by Toei and Bandai's Super Sentai Series.

I'm not really one for writing reviews, but I wanted to make an exception for Chroma Squad.
This game is an absolute gem. It is so suffused with character and charm as to reach points of ridiculousness. It pairs down the infinite complexity of many tactic games to a small team of characters, which allows each to have their own personality. The storyline, though I'm only a few hours in, is the perfect blend of cliché, kitsch, and nostalgia that somehow comes together to be more than the sum of its parts.
I can say wholeheartedly that I really wish I had seen the kickstarter when it was up so that I could say I had done my part to make this game possible.
I would be remiss if I didn't mention a few things I would've like to have seen, after all this is a review. I went in expecting to be able to make small graphical reprentation of my friends and I, but when selecting characters you select them as a whole character. So you can't choose what they look like without also choosing their stat bonuses. So, while there is character customization it's not as indepth as I would've liked.
During gameplay you'll get access to crafting. I would've liked to have seen a slightly more informative UI and perhaps an indication of how deep the crafting tree goes. It would also be nice if there was more options at each tier. As it is, it seems to break down to two options, either straight HP or HP with some added utility. But, as I said, I'm only a few hours in. (Half way through Season 3)
If those two points started to scare you away from this game, please don't let them. I have not had this much goofy fun in a long time, and I wouldn't want you to miss out on it because of my whining.
I unreservedly recommend this game.

I have played through the trilogy of the games, and the only thing I have to say is that I'm not very impressed.
While the gameplay of this game is certainly vastly better than the others, including proper puzzle tutorials on how the puzzle worked, I can't help but feel as though something is wrong. As though, somehow, I've been cheated out of something.
Oh, right, a respectable ending.
[Spoilers be beyond.]
This game, its script writing, and everything about it seems to revolve around puffing up the writers' and developers' ego, and focusing almost entirely on their own egocentric views as placed through the main character, and multiple references back to the game devs and writers that break the fourth wall only seem to shore up that representation. It's like what happened in Bubsy 3D, only far less charming when presented by an over the top, sexist, egocentric madman, who, until the very end, was the same worthless bag of trash until he finally found a reason to sacrifice himself. Even then, we didn't get that saddening, emotional ending that would have left everyone satisfied with the series on a whole, and willing to close the book. Somehow, an editor boards the ship and ends up falling with Rufus just to break that tragic ending with more self centered egotism.
If this had been some character like Deadpool, I might have made an exception. But it's not. He was not shown as some bad♥♥♥♥♥chopping his way through those that opposed him while making sly comments and breaking the fourth wall. No, he was a bumbling fool who stumbled through danger and solved menial puzzles, caused suicides and death, nearly causes the destruction of his home planet three times, puts his friends in immeasurable danger, and at the very end, when we finally get to feel sad and sorry to see him go? We're not even given that.
You know, the worst part of this game wasn't really Rufus, though he was the character that said it, it was how the writers decided to approach sexism. To the point where talking to any female who is not Goal became an ear grating experience, and not just from listening to Toni either. Rufus, and the way he talked to females, most notably regarding Bambina and Lottie outside the tank, was disgusting, and over the top for even Rufus. It felt like the writers at that point weren't calling out how bad sexism is, but were, and likely still are, sexist themselves!
Now let's talk about another part of this game. Cloans. Really? ... Actually, that's not that bad, no.
It was Hermes. I took one look at him and I said "Star Child." For those of you who have played the Mass Effect series, who know how bad of a taste those two words leave in your mouth, then you must see exactly what I mean. He was the cop out. He was the "I have all the solutions to all of your problems!" guy. While I will admit that his exposition certainly did make some of the mysteries of the trilogy fall into place, we then follow it all up by having him commit suicide. Oh bravo, BRAVO! Way to touch on that situa- Wait, did I say touch?
No, once again, the writers, or perhaps not them, perhaps someone higher up was "touching base" with them constantly and telling them what to write. Either way, the writers blatantly show another facet of suicide later on (rope noose store) and even have a therapist suggest one of his patients kill herself. I'm sorry, but what happens if someone who suffers from severe clinical depression picked this up, played it, and saw that? Do you really think some people aren't going to be affected by that? I mean, as someone who, at one point in his life, had to deal with those tendencies, it's horribly offensive, to say the least. Not that I'm claiming the writers ever came up with any tact regarding insults no matter the character those insults came from, or what or who they were about.
But I can't deny this game having its moments. Romance between Goal and Rufus was certainly charming, to say the least. Finally seeing Bozo snap and slap the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of Rufus was also very, very nice. Seeing his "father" unravel himself in front of everyone else, seeing Rufus finally get his time under the spotlight, and truly having their support for one, final plan... That was finally a moment of heroism when it was never even once allowed before even when the PLAYER wanted to make a right decision in the series. Oh, and you thought I forgot about that.
Oh no, this is something that NEEDS to be touched on, even if it wasn't a big problem in this game. Stopping the player from making the right choice, and instead taking that option from our hands. That is just disgustingly pitiful, and a clear show of a lack of effort there. Nothing gets me angrier than when my ability to decide a key moment means nothing in that moment. It's not funny, it's just a disgusting way to allow the writers to slack.
So, all in all, can I recommend this trilogy to to other people on the internet? It highly depends. If you like puzzle games, and don't give a rat's♥♥♥♥♥about the story, please, get this trilogy in the full. The puzzles are actually quite fun once you understand them, and often very well crafted. The story is ruined by the characters, the comedy does not exist outside of some slapstick moments, and the twists are oh-so-predictable.
Finally, I have to include one last bit. I'm not an SJW, and I will never be. I don't want anything that I've said to be thrown under their banner, even though I know half of it will. What I said in this review is entirely of my own opinion, and only my own. I touched on the things that felt like they were well over the top, even for a character like Rufus. I enjoyed the gameplay, which was quite honed and well made, but I could hardly stand more than a few characters in the game. This is not a book I close with contentment, but with contempt. Good day to you all, I need to get some sleep.

Evolve is a 4v1 competitive first-person cooperative shooter by Turtle Rock Studios (creators of Left 4 Dead).  The game offers challenging levels of competitive gameplay pitting 4 hunters against 1 monster in a hostile environment.  The hunters have four classes: trapper, support, medic, and assault.  There are currently 3 monsters in the game: goliath, kracken, and wraith with a forth monster (bohemoth) to be released soon. Monsters are designed similar to classes with melee, caster, and tank like abilities. Those that deal more damage have less health.  The classes of monsters and combination of hunter classes play out as being well balanced so long as groups work together.  But teamwork and communication become vital to continued success.
The game is built on the 4th generation of the CryEngine and looks great.  This is one of the best looking games this year.  The game plays very smooth but I have noticed some tearing in cut scenes and frame drops on some maps with max settings.
Games can end quickly or not depending on the skill level of the players.  Each class has a purpose and should be played to that purpose to win.  The environment alone can kill you if you venture off on your own.  This game stresses teamwork by design.  The community so far has been good although with a competitive game like this you can expect some less than mature behavior at times.
The game has received a lot of negative reviews concerning the DLC market.  The DLC in my honest opinion should have little to do with the rating of this game due to not only the design of the game but the DLC model.  The game has been designed to allow DLC content to not prohibit gamers from playing any game mode or maps.  The DLC offered will eventually add new personalities and monsters to the game but is not required to play with or against people with the DLC.  The majority of DLC consists of skins for monsters and hunters alike with a small amount being playable characters that will mix abilities of a class with a new look and personality.
Unlike many other AAA titles, Evolve does not restrict your ability to play the game with the exception of the characters not being playable without purchasing the DLC.  The alternative would be to add map packs and game modes that would cut the player base down to those that have the DLC and those that do not rather than the current DLC model that gives maps and modes to the community for free and charges for nonessential content.  It would have been nice to have had some skins rewarded for unlocks but that isn't the case, at least at this time.
The developers have put a lot of time balancing this game and it shows.  This game is a lot of fun and if you are a fan of cooperative games like Left 4 Dead, this may be right up your alley.  I have linked an older video from Alpha of my first impressions, not much has changed.  You can follow my link to my Steam page or my YouTube page for current gameplay if you like.

Once and for all: I know that many do not agree with the business practices of Turtle Rock and 2K. In particular, the preorder monster and the skins you can and will find in the ingame shop. I do also think it grossly exaggerated. A skin for € 2.99 ?? Never ever! This is almost a kebab (without health risks)!
For those who do not know, Evolve is "cops and robbers" with monster and space soldiers. You play a predefined group of mercenaries or the monster. You must complete various missions per round. That monster can, by feeding, "evolve" up to three evolutionary stages and acquire new skills. The mercenary can be revived up to two times. No, they do not evolve...but every faction gains new skills by completing skill challenges.
So is "Evolve" any fun? Yes! But the only question is, "How long?"
After a few rounds you have seen it all. But this is it for every multiplayer game out there. Which is not an apology. I think the variation lies within the players and the vast enviroment. For me thats enough...for €40 - 60€. Why?
There are groups that act tactically. They are using the enviroment, plan ahead and lure the Monster into a trap. Then there are groups which are rushing toward against. Some groups split up and others stubbornly pursue the mission objective, that is defined in each round, so they achieve a victory this way. You will forget that there are just a handful of maps to explore. You really do not notice.
And the environment is harmonious and just beautiful. Every detail has been placed with love. Kudos to the level designers! A moody and mostly believable game world. I guess thats the true content of Evolve. This is sometimes better than 30 sloppy maps.
In summary, I can only say that I previously had fun with Evolve. It plays well, offers interesting possibilities in terms of tactical diversity and movement. It's polished, despite a few bugs. The characters are not quite as loveable as the Left4Dead protagonists. I'm curious what Turtle Rock does next with Evolve. I hope the skins are getting cheaper...come on guys! You don't need that much money.
As for the REAL long-term motivation, I can't say anything yet. Maybe the few maps and missions ARE the problem? Or  it gets boring after you've unlocked every single♥♥♥♥♥♥ Perhaps it turns out that the the balancing is aweful after more and more players reach the higher levels? Nobody knows.
Buy it if you have friends to play with or if you are like that kid from the "ready or not trailer" who plays the monster.

I simply wish there were more Star Wars RTS games out there like Empire at War. Don't be confused by the storyline, it's not "canon" or adheres to the lore 100% but the gameplay is what sells me. I'm a huge Star Wars nuthead but when I came across the Galactic Map and all the planets I could conquer it seemed quite daunting.
You take over worlds with 2 fleets, the first fleet is your "Space Fleet", which invades an enemy planet and initiates a space battle. Should you win this battle (and destroy the enemy space station / fleet) you can send your second fleet, namely "Ground Forces". This will initiate a tactical land battle whereby you have to destroy all the enemy structures, capture reinforcement points in order to increase you unit cap on the map (therefore more ground forces can land) and do this with every planet.
The large amount of units to choose from, different routes to take and with the addition of the Pirate Faction in Forces of Corruption (the expansion) you'll find that you're in for a really long and great time. The AI is ruthless on harder difficulties and the game is mod compatible so do check out the Empire at War Filefront website for huge add-ons to the game.
At this point I guess I've clocked 400+ hours on this, and that's just a small estimate, I'm certain it's a LOT more. Check the game out, see videos of it online, do what you want but I highly recommend this game.

Braveland Pirates is a hexagonal turn based strategy game. It is the third of a three part adventure offered by Tortuga Team, exploring the adventures of different characters in the world. I have played and reviewed the original game in this trilogy, and I found it to be a small, enjoyable game with a tight knit story that drew me in, and a balanced gameplay with a solid, strong hero. The same, unfortunately, can not be said for Braveland Pirates.
The overall impression I got of this game was that they tried to expand upon their original idea, and overshot it. You play as a pirate that travels to various islands in order to collect pieces of a map which lead you to a legendary treasure. Other than that, the dialogues, companions and storytelling doesn't build into feeling like a pirate, or the captain of your crew. None of the story adds any depth into feeling like a pirate adventure. The units you work with and unlock throughout the game do not hold up tactically to the increase in difficulty as you progress. There are some exceptions to this rule, as I go over in the video review ,but in addition, when you enter later stages of the game, you are limited as to what units are available, and are forced to use some units simply because you have no other option due to lack of balance in between the units. The lack of units that are available also means that you are fighting many, many battles with the same units.
When there are limited troops available, and therefore limited mechanics, this adds to the feeling of grinding or repetition throughout the battles. It falls to the strength of the story to pull the player into the game, and unfortunately, this game has failed in that aspect, as the story is poorly written and structured. The hero does have talents that he can earn throughout the game, but these talents which can be useful, lack any feeling of power as you level up, it is felt more through the gear and weapons that you pick up.
I do not fault the game for being simple in its style or mechanics, but I feel that there needed to be certain adjustments to the hero, the troops and the mechanics in order feel like a flushed out game of this size. The game did not respect my time. Even on the hardest setting, the difficulty is a joke! As long as you have a basic knowledge of this style of genre, that is. The main times I had any trouble was situational to do the really bad balance at some points. You are limited in your hero's development, and in the support units you choose. I wanted to like this game, and went into it expecting a continuation of the experience I had in the first game. Instead I felt that my time was wasted.

After not-so-good Wizard, Braveland Pirate is surprisingly good, even if borrows heavely from Katauri's King Bounty.
Probably the most improtant change for me is that the balance of the strength of your enemies and the amount of gold earned now makes way more sense, if compared to the previous installment. That was the biggest problem with Wizard, and in Pirate it is evidently properly taken care about.
But changes, and most of them to the good, are numerous. You hero is now represented with a unit on the battlefield, which in theory limits your choice of troops to be taken with, but I haven't found it to be a hindrance. The hero unit is, on the other side, quite useful and perfectly serves both as a damage dealer and a magnetic absorber of enemies' ranged attacks. The hero attibutes do not affect the army anymore, which is not much of loss, since they their bonuses were neglectable anyway. Instead they affect the hero unit only, which works fine with artefacts now being many and mostly useful. The levelcap has also been increased to level 15.
Recruitable units are now grouped into pools, with units from each pool being available for hire in any one of tavern network scattered around, which saves you quite some time. Dungeons now have limits, which is fine for me as well.
There are quite a few other new interesting features introduced, but I'll stop here, and let you discover by yourself.
Overall, the best thing of all is that the game feels now much more solid, mature and well-designed, if compared with the prior parts. It is evident, that this time the developers have put a notable amount of effort into improving and polishing of the game, and I'd say that they have definetely succeded.

Welcome to the game that made me poor as a kid!!!
It was originally released in 1984 a year after 'dragon lair' and followed the same principle that being a laser disc arcade. 'Laser Disc' technology was like the 'future' back then and playing a game like this would make a kid feel like he was time travelling into the future of gaming. Oh what little we knew!
Like its predecessor its art style was all thanks to Don Bluth who worked on masterpiece animation films such as 'The American Tale' and the 'Land before time' amongst other great works. Like FMV games today, the novelty of controlling a cartoon by moving a hero around the screen away from incoming danger was a popular trend. However ‘Space Ace’ added another dynamic which ‘Dragon's Lair’ did not have. Not only was the objective to move your main character in the direction of provisional yellow flashes, or to hit the shoot button when the heroes gun flashed yellow, but now you could also occasionally change the main character to an older version of himself changing the dynamics and pathway of that adventure which provided even more animation fun and a very large number of novelty death scenes.
Problem was though that 'Space Ace' was never as popular as 'Dragon's Lair' and people wanted more of that than they did a sudden mock up. No one really knew where the concept of Space Ace came from? The Game unfortunately may have seemed too 'Alien' for some of the general public.
In truth though, there was a very old adult comic back in 1952 named 'Space Ace' and personally I thought some of the concepts were very loosely based on that. In that comic 'Ace' is a Marshall who has been hired to protect Earth against interstellar crimes, but other than that the game seems to be as different from the comic as chalk and cheese. Let me illustrate...
The VG itself informs us the story about Kimberly and Dexter both Officer and Marshal hired to protect the Earth against interstellar crime. Borf a hideous looking alien smurf with a face yelling amphetamines and yet a belly screaming couch potato, has got himself an infanto-ray which as the name suggests is a deadly ray that can make anything it hits younger. Borf plans to use it against the planet Earth if Earth does not surrender itself to Borf's total control. Borf shows that he isn't joking either by immediately performing a test run of the infanto-ray changing our unsuspecting hero 'Ace' back to his younger self 'Dexter'. While Ace likes to shoot things first and ask questions later and likes to get himself into punch-ups, Dexter on the other hand lacks any hero experience and has to simply rely on running away and dodging trouble. To make matters worse Borf also kidnaps our sidekick Kimberly leaving the planet Earth vulnerable with no hero in sight.
The original manual that came with the arcade stated that Dexter had a unique connection with unknown cosmic forces which enabled him to momentarily reverse the effects of the infanto-ray and become his alter ego again known as Ace, and other than that, the VG and manual offered no other explanation. While the game could never be taken seriously thanks to its assortment of wild shenanigans of diverse creatures and robots, there was never any introductions to such enemies or main characters. Hence because everything just seemed to magically appear and disappear just as quick, there was no real emotional attachment ever invested in such characters.
There was a real earnest effort to try and improve the games popularity by spawning in a season of 'Space Ace' cartoons that were to be showcased on Saturday Supercade, but other than 13 episodes it never went on for a second season. Also a new Space Ace comic was released, but other than a very few rare to find now copies, even the new comic never really went anywhere.
Still if anyone has seen interviews with Don Bluth then they would know that Space Ace holds a special part in his heart as much as it does with many nostalgic retro gamers. And if you want a history lesson then this is a good place to start.
To get the most out of your experience I strongly suggest this, there is an achievement in game where you have to try and complete the game in Ace mode (hardest difficulty) with no movement hints. This is how it was when the original arcade came out. Keep a tally of how many times you had to continue your five lives. Now remember that the original arcade to play was $2.00, so multiply that cost by the amount of times you had to continue and that was your history of arcade gaming.
One last thing to make your mind seriously go WTH. The cartoon series that spawned after the VG revealed that Dexter and Kimberly are brother and sister. Now reflect on the motor bike scene in this game. HMMMMM!? Cringe!!! However, it is unlikely that any of these interesting titbits will be known to any newcomer to this game which seriously makes we wish for a 'Definitive Collection' of 'Space Ace', which should include not only this version, but even all the other versions which are quite different, but based on the same principle, for example the snes version. This collection could also include the 13 cartoons and even the comics that spawned thereafter. That’s the collection that the fans of 'Space Ace' truly deserve.

Graphically this game is going places, but it suffers with many of the same problems of other survival simulators.
1. Your need for food, water, rest, etc decrease too quickly
- As an avid outdoors enthusiast I'm put put off by the haste games make-believe how fast someone can fatigue in this sort of weather. What really shocks me is you can sprint to exhaustion, but not suffer sweats (and the resultant hypothermia) while walking at an even pass that should be warming your body to the extent you are losing heat you actually start to freeze
2. Most the experience of survival is wasted on basically being in a desperate search for restoring one of your stat metrics which (again) shouldn't be going down so fast at all. This would have be an extremely inexperienced person OR the weather conditions is so unreasonable that hypothermia is inevitable.
3. Points two and three create the sense of "ahh f~it, best to just to get this over with," where upon you find your sleeping back, crawl into it and go to 'sleep' timing it out so hypothermia sets you into unconsciousness while you're not awake.
Anyway, great atmosphere, but it's just another game of "go get said resource" that just depletes every half hour no matter how you pace yourself or set your mind. Games just can't do this kind of thing well.

1st person, action, shooter. A whole under water city gone mad, aka Rupture Asylum and genocide on the freaks that live there. Personally I didn't like the story at all. It's pretty much about people with power that wanted everything to be perfect. Then they got bored of it and started doing sick stuff to each other.
Plasmids aka the 'super powers' add additional sickness to everything on top, plus the little girls used as harvesters for substance called Adam, that power all the Plasmids. The only humane thing in the game I found, was to save the little girls and help their 'mother' throughout the game, that felt right to do. And apart from her and girls I didn't really find any other positive character. Wont spoil any story, but it wasn't as good as I hoped.
For an old game it looked decent, nothing major. Gun play felt very basic though there are many guns available. Enemies were pretty much all humans that were abused by plasmids or experiments, torture, etc., one way or another. Some had interesting abilities in form of vanish / invisibility, walking on walls / ceiling, etc.. AI was challenging, dodging shots, rushing you on, flanking.
Plasmid selection was insane and they were fun to use. Looting and hacking was also very enjoyable. After a while game started to drag on, missions and tasks were tedious with all the do this and do that constantly, it felt like I was literally mind controlled in real life. And right after the "Golf scene", I got bored completely.
Character design and animations were above average, but nothing good. Visually I guess game was good for it's time, but don't expect much. Voice acting was good and enjoyable. Though I didn't enjoy much of the story, I still recommend this because some people might find it more entertaining than I did. To close this off, for me Bioshock Infinite had far more enjoyable story than this, though they are connected in some way.

In the world of 'Rapture', it's ruined. It's a city that's underwater with the purpose of inviting men ( & weman) into a world where they live for themselves. Set in ther 1960's, everything in Rapture takes the theme, style, music, and he general atmosphere of the american years where a man is measured his money, and the amount of alcohol and cigarettes he puts in himself. That was rapture before everything brokedaown with the peoples' brain and genetic/DNA codes.
The world of Rapture, now, is broken. no laws. no equality, no humanity; just theft, gun fight, and the place itself will constantly aim to end itself; for the survival of the fitest. There are recordings of what Raptures was like before, but in audio form, some are happy others....
You play as a victim of a certain tragity and end up in Rapture in there later years. And after a quick view of the city, you the people directly infront of you. yeah, very hostile. The game is a First Person Shooter where you survive, battle, raid, and the gimmick for this game, Gene upgrades. Your right handed gunner and left handed wizard with have to go through this corupted city which gradualy get worse and worse, to find your way out while being guided by a man in your ear who wants to do the same.
You are alone in this cluster of steal with your weapons, unrealistic genetic powers, your wits and will, and your ability and use the environment of rapture to help you defend yourself. You must kill, find money and aid kits, Mana/Eve, and amunition. Your main objective is to escape Rapture in one peice, but you can still explore to find loot, recordings and rarely, genetic upgrades.
Your gene upgrade is what makes battle interesting, it can be an escape plan, for something to turn the tables around, but you can only hold a few at a time. The more you advance, the more you can find, that also goes weapons & their upgrades.
I'm not gong to go deep into the plot or the plot points or some of the events because I wamt you face them. Oh boy here it is Chroma Squad. A game like no other out there.
Let me start of by saying that this is a game for children.
Nothing for adults like me and you. We are big now. We can buy alcohol, drive and get on all roller coasters.
I mean I pretty much watched Power Rangers and the likes whenever I could, because well
... err I mean I was forced to watch it.
Anyway you don't have to be a fan of Tokusatsu and Sentai to fully enjoy this game. I mean it doesn't hurt if you are it probably makes everything just so much better but all you need to fully enjoy it is a sense of humor.
Chroma Squad is a Tactical-Management-Business-RPP about running your very own sentai show.
You slip into the role of five stuntmen which basically got fed up that they do pretty much all the work while the actors are just sitting in their chairs most of the time. One comes up with the idea to create their own studio and so they quit their jobs to set up their own sentai studio.
This game is filled with jokes and references to the tv shows or to memes and it's overall a very good laugh.
You now have to setup your studio and buy props like mics, lamps or a better green screen. Those items will give you all special bonuses but also come for a price. You don't only have to pay once for those items well for some you do and others cost something like 25 bucks each episode. So you have to choose wisely on what to upgrade. Also you have to hire actors, choose an agency to help you reach a greater audience and make sure you're fans are happy since hey this is tv show!
In case it wasn't obvious but you take the role of five actors and the director of your sentai tv show. You have to read and reply to fan mail which can grant you bonuses depending on your actions and then there's crafting.
Duct tape, play dough, card boxes and many more stuff you'll need to craft your new items like swords, guns, helmets and so on. You can buy several materials and you can also recycle your old and unused gear for materials. You only have a % chance to get certain materials but hey atleast you have the chance to get some materials back.
Your goal is to record five episodes for a season. Meaning you have to record and fight five different scenarios before you reach the season finale aka end boss battle. While recording the shows you see the directors instructions on screen which you should follow in order to get the max amount of audience.
If you enjoy tactical and/or rpg games you should definitely give Chroma Squad a try.

Chroma Squad is simply a love letter to what Power Rangers use to be. It has action, comedy, interesting writing, and anything you would want from a PR game. You start out as 5 stuntmen who have recently quit their jobs doing sentai stunts to form their own studio. When you get into the studio thats when the real magic begins. Once there, you're able to design your own suits and mechas, something I'm sure any PR fan has dreamed of.

You're also able to respond to fan letters and control your fan market to some extent by choosing from a wide selection of advertaisment firms. When you go into battle this game is a mix of an RTS and Turn Based RPG ala Pokemon. The RTS side is used for your simple ranger battles where each class has a variety of skills at their disposal, which grow as the story progresses. You're also able to do showy finishing moves on the bosses in true sentai fashion. My only problem with the RTS board is that sometimes you can't see parts of the grid because they're blocked by objects on the field.
The game then becomes much closer to a TurnBased RPG when in mecha form where you're allowed to hit your opposing monster a certain number of times before a hit misses and they hit back. But, all is not lost when they hit back theres a system that if you time it correctly and click in the white area of the bar you can block some of the damage. Think Gears of War's reload system. Everyonce in awhile though this bar lags causing you to get hit by the full blunt of the attack without a chance to stop it.
TL;DR:The Story and writing are amazing and are VERY PR like. The RTS combat while fun has some issues with grid square blocking, nothing gamebreaking though. The mecha combat is far slower than the RTS combat but still quite fun

Having beaten this game back in the good ol' arcade days, it's a bit difficult sometimes to adhere to this version's moves and timing.  Some moves are nowhere near what the original arcade had. Really fun game with a lot of replay value.  Tactical RPG combat flows well and the team-up system leads to some fun things to do even while abilities are on cooldown.  Branching story paths make for some good incentive to play through multiple times.
Mecha battles are a little one-note, but still fun.  Crafting system seems to have bad drops, but with proper marketing choices and investing in some of the material packs you can make it work out.
My only complaints: YOU CANNOT UNDO ACTIONS, which is so frustrating sometimes, oh boy.  That's the number one problem for me.  Also there is not enough cool stuff to spend money on in the in-game store, as each tier boils down to "defense armor" vs "offense armor".  Crafting has one or two interesting items (the Speed boots and the Team-Toss gloves) but there isn't a lot of variety outside of the gimmick items, when there could be a lot more going on.  More actor choices (and the ability to recast them mid-series) would be nice too, it feels like a very small pool of options.
The game also ends right when you start feeling very powerful so I'd like to see a 'New Series' mode (where you do a new team with a new storyline but keep your studio) or some sort of extra seasons.  Some way to keep going.  The game feels a little short.  A 'mission creator' and some sort of endless mode with escalating difficulty as seasons keep going on could fix this, and I believe the developers are looking into these sorts of ideas.
It's off to a great start, it's an awesome game for anyone into tactical RPGs or sentai/power rangers stuff, and I hope it keeps improving over time.

The Journey Down is so ernest and genuine, you can't help but love it.
TJD is a classic 3D point and click adventure in the vein of something like Grim Fandango. You usually have a given task to do, and you have to go around collecting seemingly unrelated items and using them to solve various puzzles to progress through the game. TJD uses "adventure game logic", which means that you can't use a mop to shoo away a pesky pelican, but you can stuff a fish with chilli peppers and then get the pelican to eat the fish, causing it to faint (from the spiciness). You see where I'm going with this? There is nothing wrong with that, however. It's a fun genre trope that brings me back to the days of the classic Monkey Island games.
I'm not gonna talk much about the story, there are some interesting things here and there, but really it's the characters that make this game shine. Every character in the game has their own "thing" going on, making them amusing, though slightly 1 dimensional at times. The main charcter, Bwana, stands out as a very likeable guy that is very genuine and good-natured. You can't help but laugh at his interactions with others, especially those that know him well, like his brother.
Two somewhat related flaws with this game: 1. The puzzles are very easy to solve IF you have experience playing these kinds of games and are familiar with "adventure game logic". There was only one puzzle that had me stumped, but for most others it really comes down to finding the right item and knowing what to do with it. Which leads me to # 2. The game is very short. Took me 2-3 hours to finish this chapter, probably due to how easy the puzzles were.
Still, I highly recommend this game if you wanna have a fun afternoon playing an honest point&click adventure game. I will certainly play chapter 2 at some point in the near future.

Goodbye Deponia is a humoristic point n' click adventure game that tries and succeeds at emulating the old style of LucasArts' games of old, mainly Day of The Tentacle and such.
The graphics are absolutely beautiful, the backgrounds and characters are hand drawn, but the animations aren't, making it feel like the animation style of modern cartoons made in Flash. Don't get me wrong, it still looks gorgeous, but the animations might seem a little robotic at times.
The gameplay is pretty much what you'd expect from a game like this, you use your mouse 100%, you click to move, gathering new items and objects to solve puzzles and you talk to people to hint at a puzzle solution or to advance the game's progress, sometimes the character conversations themselves are puzzles to solve.
Speaking of wich, the puzzles aren't too obtuse or cryptic, but keep in mind that you also have to mix up certain items to make progress. This game also has plenty of minigames to break from the normal point n' click stuff and they get really weird really fast, with the next one even more outrageous than the last.
It gets a little complex by the mid point, because you start controlling 2 clones of yourself at the same time, going as far as to interchange items between the three, wich is actually a really neat idea, just keep in mind that you need to keep track of who's having wich item.
The sound design is a little hit or miss, the music is okay, conveying the right mood for the room or situation you're in, the sounds are okay too, but the voice acting is a little hit or miss for me, most of the voice acting sounds good in my opinion, at least for comedic purposes, as most of them sound ridiculous and exaggerated, but there are a few times where you just can't hear what they're saying for how low their volume is, making the use of subtitles a must.
And finally the story. Going in blind and without previous knowledge about the previous games didn't deterr the experience for me, although it probably would've helped to get to know certain characters better, because they do reference the past games A LOT, but not so much as not to enjoy the third game on it's own.
The character of Rufus is what will make or break the game for some, he does a lot of despicable stuff, like making the lives of certain characters a miserable living hell, he whines a friggin' lot and some of his lines can get very annoying very fast. I know it's intended to not be taken seriously, but come on, leaving children to their fate on a monster infested sewer did make me rise an eyebrow, is this really the guy we're supposed to root for?
The ending left a bit of a sour taste in my mouth, but not so much as to ruin the game.
All in all, if you've played the previous games, you'd probably already know if you want to play this or not, especially considering this is the conclusion of the trilogy, just adjust your expectations for the ending. And for people who haven't played the series before, I'd say you're better off starting from the first game and play them sequentially, BUT if for any reason you only have or bought this game, then go ahead and play it!
It really is a lot of fun! =)
