I was surprised when I booted up this game to see no compatibility issues whatsoever on my modern machine. Considering that I've played games half it's age that have issues with Windows 10, I guess something you have to take into account when you buy old games off steam, so being able to jump right in was refreshing, to say the least. Of course the game came out in 2006 so minimum requirements are as low as my life prospects, so my prediction is that most things will run it hitch-free. The thought of playing this on something like a GPD Win (Nintendo DS sized Intel atom PC with Xbox controls, look it up) is so believable and would work so well it makes me almost a bit giddy.
A lot of the existing reviews mention that they bought the game mainly due to nostalgia of playing this game on their Xbox or PS2 back in 2006, which is probably why you're on the store page right now. My flavour was a pirated copy of the PSP port Flatout: Head-On. Many hours in my single-digit years were wasted on that, so immediately as I kick into the game I notice some differences in presentation between these two, which is expected. Obviously the graphics have taken a notch up, and the image quality of everything in general looks much better than it did on the PSP (Lord bless its soul). So the nostalgia train was not only rolling at that point but being tied to a jet engine.
What threw me off was that there is actually quite a bit of content for what would have been somewhat of a "AAA" game. This is when I reminded myself that this was back in a time when extra content wasn't tacked on for extra money, or baited in front of your eyes in the menus and selection screens. Obviously if DLC was as widespread as it was in 2006 they would probably still be using it, but the variety of modes, cars and minigames keeps interest high, as well as the amount of time engaged in the game. However none of the content feels like fluff or bloat, and all has some sort of appeal to it, even if it's not the main highlight, which is also something more modern games need to learn. This is what makes nostalgia. The turn-out for the good game:bad game ratio must have been much better back in the day....

I would like to preface this by saying I will only talk about the game, not TRS or anything involving business practices. I bought the game shortly after the Beta, after putting 60 hours into it between the Alpha and Beta. I got the Monster Race edition for $70 (This deal has ended).
Pros
+ Balanced Asymmetric Warfare
It takes finesse, skill, and a hell of a lot of time to balance teams that are inherently uneven, but Evolve has managed to straddle that peak. Both sides are fun to play as, and require vastly different skillets to be successful in, providing twice the game you would expect from an online-multiplayer shooter. Naturally, there was a lot of talk during the Alpha about the Kraken being OP, and during the Beta, the Wraith received similar treatment, but TRS has been actively balancing the game, and it feels much more even as of release. The game feels fair, and either side has just as good a chance of winning, with a slight caveat discussed in Cons.
+ Good Variety in characters
Each playable character in each role feels very distinct from the others, and I think this is best captured in the medic class. Val, Lazarus, and Caira all preform the same function, they keep the team alive, but the way in which they do it is so drastically different. Val can affix a beam of healing energy on a target, guaranteeing health over time. Caira has to be more careful with her healing, firing shots that explode in an area of healing, giving the potential to miss and having to worry about reloading. Lazarus operates on a complete paradigm shift of healing, instead of directly healing his teammates, he instead nullifies one of the biggest penalties of being incapped, not healing per say, but accomplishing the goal of keeping the team functioning.
+ Replayability
Evolve has a very simple formula. 4v1 Hide-and-go-seek, some would argue that that reduces replay ability, but I think it increases it. Think of COD, Halo, Battlefield or any other online multiplayer game (Outside of MMOs). All of them have very relative game-modes. 4v4, get 50 kills. And yet some forget that those games are very repayable, because even though the goal is the same every time, no two matches are the same. And Evolve holds that moniker well.
Cons
- Reliance on Teamwork
This is not a bad thing, hell I would say this is the mark of a solid multiplayer game. However, it can be said that if the monster knows what they are doing, you NEED solid teamwork from the hunters to make the fight fair. This means communication, which I have had a good amount of teammates not use the voice chat, or even the text. Naturally these games mostly ended in defeat. If you want to play a hunter, you have to work together, so use voice chat.
- Wall Climbing
This is a very specific complaint, but it has annoyed me enough to warrant a spot here. One way the hunters don't get completely outpaced by the monster is the ability to climb walls without jetpack fuel. However, this fails about half the time, and I hit a wall about 80% to the top, only to not climb, and have to hit ground before it will let me try again. And with some of the complex geometry of walls in the game, this can completely kill your chase.
- Progression, now with buffs!
One thing that has bothered me about online games is the idea that, time spent in a game can overpower skill at the game. You can be better at someone in COD, but if they have a better load out, they have a significant advantage. This is something i've come to accept as inevitable in gaming, as the allure of progression and "becoming more powerful" is one of the main draws that games use to keep people playing. But every time I queue up as monster and see a squad of 1's and 2's as my opponents, I know immediently that I am going to win. They may be very strong players, but I have access to more powerful buffs, (30% cool down on Kraken, good ♥♥♥♥ing luck) and they are stuck with basic buffs and only the first tier of hunters. Speaking of, the biggest complaint I have about the game, is that with such DIVERSITY among even the classes of hunters, why lock them behind a progression system. Bucket is a vastly different support then Hank, and I love Bucket, hate Hank. So why make me play upwards of 10 games as Hank to get Access to Bucket? I think that diversity in the game needs to be expressed, not locked. How does playing Goliath make me a better Kraken player? Wraith? These monsters are so uniquely different in their play styles, that a large portion of understanding is not transferrable.
There is obviously a lot more to say about this game, but these are a summation of SOME, not all, of my biggest points for, and against, Evolve as of release.

This is my first time with this kind of TD (so I can't compare to WC3/SC2/DOTA2), and I have to say, I'm in love.
For those like me who are new to the genre, here's an overview:
Legion TD2 is a "competitive tower defense" game. 2 teams of 4 fight against identical waves, defending their team's King from creeps. The game is split into two phases, night and day. During the night, you place, upgrade, and sell towers, and hire mercenaries. During the day, your towers wake up to defend various waves of creeps (sent by the game) and mercenaries (sent by your opponents).
Currently there are 4 races (or legions), and one legion using random units from each other legion. It appears the devs are planning on adding more races, cosmetics, and mod support. However, the dev team is only 2 people, so I would expect mostly bugfixes and balancing to come before new features.
Currently, I would be catious about recommending the game.  It's fun, but $20 is pretty steep for what is currently a glorified mod. Keep your eye on it. Any sale above 25% off should be an insta-buy, and maybe in half a year, once more features are added, it'll be a must have. Or, if you've played counltess hours of WC3 Legion TD (as it seems many have), you shoudl grab it to support the devs.
edit: Being a new player, I was very skeptical of jumping straight into multiplayer, bu the community is really helpful. Even though most players are from Germany, many speak good enough english to help if you have any questions.  Streamers, as few as they are, are also very helpful, and were invaluable for helping me learn the game.  This is probably the most friendly and helpful community I've ever seen. Unfortunately, it's the only real way to learn the game, as there is no tutorial, and very few good videos that cover anything beyond the basics.
edit2: Ratings have been enabled, as have achievements, etc. Still only PVP, no custom games or v bots. In addition, there is no unranked PVP. I still recommend this game, been having a great time.
